assumptions: Snapshot/restore is a lifecycle and durability feature, so stale/invalid snapshot handling, CRC/invariant failure, and partial acceptance behavior are in scope.
Store APIs can be extended with snapshot(Path) and restore(Path) without changing publishChecked call signatures or existing builder semantics.
Snapshot files are local filesystem artifacts written atomically through a temporary file, durable flush where supported, and atomic move into place.
The guaranteed journal cursor is the source of truth for acknowledged writes during restore reconciliation.
Restore may allocate off the publish path, but publish, publishChecked, and read hot paths must remain allocation-neutral.
A structured invariant failure type or equivalent canonical store exception will represent invalid headers, stale cursors, CRC mismatches, and partial snapshot rejection.

design_contract.concurrency_protocol: snapshot(Path) observes a stable store image without changing publishChecked commit ordering. restore(Path) validates all snapshot invariants off to the side, reconciles against the guaranteed journal cursor, then performs one atomic swap/install step so readers never observe half-restored pages. Restoring pages before validating header, version, dimensions, kind, cursor, and every page CRC.
Accepting staged-but-unjournaled writes after restore.
Using non-atomic overwrite of the target snapshot as the snapshot commit protocol.
Silently ignoring CRC, stale cursor, truncated file, or unsupported version failures.
hard_constraints: Zero allocation on the publish hot path remains invariant.
